items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m very pleased to have Hal Espinosa with me today. Welcome. [INTERVIEWEE] Thanks for having me on.

ctx.x: I see. I wanted to wrap up just with an observation that I’ve been noticing and that is what used to be our word, and I’m speaking of “gig” — has now become usurped in a number of ways. I remember hearing DJs start talking about, “I have a gig tomorrow.” And I remember being like don’t say that, you don’t have a gig. And now we have the gig economy which further usurps our own word.

But Monk, I remember when I was still working the guys would always say, “I’ve got this gig” at so-and-so. Especially the jazz players. “I’ve got a gig at Donte’s” or at the Lighthouse. Occasionally it would be a “job.” Job is more formal. A gig was, the guys would say that among themselves. So that terminology has been around a long time in the big cities, and the outlying areas may not have picked that up as fast, but it’s been around a long time.
Yes. Well you’ve had a fruitful career and I appreciate the stories you offered today and the information about the musicians’ union, which sometimes is misunderstood.
